svg.aria-label: Architecture of one turn. At session start, after /clear and after compaction, the SessionStart hook injects the orchestrator playbook into the main thread only; subagents do not receive it. When a message the user typed mentions production mode, the UserPromptSubmit hook adds one line to the main thread on how to set and unset a repository's production mark. The main thread sends a brief to a subagent, which works from its definition in agents/*.md, which sets its reasoning effort, together with CLAUDE.md and the brief, and returns a bounded report. Every tool call from either thread passes PreToolUse before the tool runs: it denies nested dispatch inside subagents, git commit --no-verify, calls that would print a secret value, direct writes to HANDOFF.md, and a researcher or retriever subagent changing, moving or deleting an existing file, while researcher and retriever subagents may still read files, run commands and create new files; a gh pr merge in a repository marked as production waits until the user approves it on the spot. A denial sends its reason back to the calling thread, which tries another way; an allowed call runs the tool. After the tool runs, PostToolUse returns a rule-file reminder as added context to the calling thread when a rule file was edited, and when a new worktree is entered it symlinks CLAUDE.md, node_modules and .env* from the main checkout into that worktree without replying. When the main thread tries to end the turn, the Stop hooks run, and if all pass the turn ends. Two of them are synchronous gates. The context watermark gate adds a reminder once per session over 35%, or on every turn when the session has no scratchpad, and lets the stop pass, blocks once over 40%, or on every turn when the session has no scratchpad, and after that blocks again at every further rise of 5 points over the usage at its last block; the reply gate blocks once when the reply's last sentence offers a next step. A block by either of these two gates returns control to the main thread. After the reply gate it either takes the offered step or, when the decision really is the user's, asks again with the background, the consequences of each option and a recommendation. After the watermark gate's first block it finishes any wrap-up that the context it already holds can complete, and when a new large block of work comes next it runs the handoff skill, in which a researcher subagent drafts HANDOFF.new.md and finalize.sh puts it in place as the handoff file, and tells the user to switch to a new session; after each further block it generates the handoff at once. A new session reads that file to carry on. Neither synchronous gate blocks the turn it has just blocked and resumed, so a single attempt to stop is blocked at most once and that turn's next attempt passes; the watermark gate still blocks again in later turns as usage rises. The third Stop hook, the keepalive gate, never blocks the stop: it runs in the background after the turn has ended, and once the main thread's context has reached 150,000 tokens and 50 minutes pass with no new turn, it wakes the main thread to reply with only a full stop, which keeps the one-hour prompt cache warm while the user is away; each wake-up starts the next timer, until 8 hours have passed since the user's own last message.

subagents may only create new files
